text:
serena: Thanks everyone for joining the town hall earlier. Dropping a follow-up thread for a couple quick asks about merit buckets, comp timing, and the PTO policy note.
jamal: quick q — if someone's promotion was flagged but not applied in this cycle, is there a retro raise / backpay? :thinking: 
mike: also — can we get an example of what 'consistent high impact' means for L4->L5 leveling? engineering managers are getting pings.
alex: high level: promotions that missed a cycle will be reviewed and, where approved, applied with retroactive pay to the effective promotion date. Not every case will qualify; we'll rely on calibration notes. Expect outreach from People Ops if you were affected.
serena: @jamal correct — the policy is "retro on approval to the effective date" for cases where calibration approved promotion but payroll cut didn't process. We'll publish the checklist and timeline by EOD Friday. :paperclip: 
peopleops-bot: uploaded a file: compensation-calibration-checklist.pdf
jamal: thanks — timeline for when managers will get final merit buckets? teams are planning salary conversations.
serena: managers will receive final merit buckets and guidance on May 6 (two weeks). Calibration memos go out May 3. Please don't finalize conversations before managers receive their packet.
mike: can you share the weighting used in calibration? i.e., how much is manager score vs peer vs product impact?
serena: summary: manager assessment 55%, peer/partner feedback 20%, objective metrics (OKR results, delivery) 15%, calibration committee adjustment 10%.
serena: Here's a compact rubric we used in calibration:
```
Leveling rubric (excerpt):
- L4: delivers consistently; owns features end-to-end; mentors peers
- L5: drives multi-team initiatives; shapes architecture; measurable product impact
- Evidence: PRs + postmortem ownership + customer impact
``` 
alex: on comp pool size — we are keeping the same total merit pool % as last year (4.5%) but focusing distribution to reward sustained high impact and critical retention cases. We'll share high-level ranges in the packet.
jamal: PTO clarification — in all-hands mention about "unlimited" vs "flex" policy caused confusion. what's the practical rule for managers approving extended leaves?
serena: good flag. We use 'flex' — it's not literally unlimited. Approvals should consider team coverage and role-critical periods. For leaves > 4 weeks, talk to People Ops early; for parental leave, statutory policies apply plus company top-up (details in benefits hub).
mike: will there be a central tracker for conversations so managers don't overlap / double offer?
serena: yes — managers will log conversations in the People Ops tracker (link in the packet). We'll also run a live Q&A next Wednesday 11am for managers only. RSVP in the calendar invite.
jamal: appreciated. one last ask — will there be communication for ICs about what to expect on comp statements? simple bullets would help.
serena: we'll send an IC-facing FAQ with examples (percentile, dollar examples, what retro pay looks like) along with manager packet. ETA: Friday.
alex: thanks everyone — we hear you. leaders will keep transparency high and follow through on the timelines above. :raised_hands: 
serena: closing notes: if you have a confidential case ping me or dm people-ops. otherwise drop issues here and we'll update the thread.
jamal: thanks, will wait for the packet.
